structural_counters.interpretation: cache never populated — every op-spec is distinct at this workload despite Python-level structural repetition across chunks. Head paid overhead without cache-hit payoff, yet dxp_standalone still improves substantially. Mechanism is canonical bundle representation shift, not spec dedup.

prediction_vs_measurement.why_prediction_missed: The static reading identified the added per-op canonical-compile + json.dumps(sort_keys=True) overhead on the frontend side but assumed cache hits would offset it. In practice, WB compiles into distinct OpSpec dicts (n_specs unchanged) despite Python-level structural repetition across chunks, so the cache never populated. Meanwhile, the canonical bundle representation shifts dxp_standalone by -40% at n=4 and -45% at n=8 — a mechanism not visible from the diff alone.

wall_clock_impact.note: Corrected in this revision — earlier impact.json used self_ns for first_call_wall and compile_fx_wrapper, which excludes nested children. inclusive_ns is the correct reduction for enclosing wall-clock stages.
